# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Puzzles

## I. By Primary Task Type

### A. Loop/Path Drawing
Puzzles where the solver draws a single continuous loop or path through the grid.

#### A1. Pure Loop Construction
- **Masyu** – Loop through cells with black/white circle constraints on turning/straight behavior
- **Slitherlink** – Loop on grid edges with numeric constraints on surrounding line counts
- **Mid-loop** – Loop through cells where black circles must be midpoints of straight segments
- **Nagareru** – Directed loop with wind constraints affecting movement
- **Moon-or-Sun** – Loop through rooms alternating between moon and sun symbols
- **Dotchi-Loop** – Loop through cells with area-based constraints on straight/turn behavior at white circles; avoids black circles
- **Suraromu** – Loop starting/ending at numbered circle, passing through all gates in order

#### A2. Loop + Cell Shading
- **Yajilin** – Loop drawn while also placing black cells; arrow clues constrain black cell counts directionally

### B. Path/Connection Drawing
Puzzles where the solver draws paths connecting specific points (not necessarily loops).

- **Numberlink** – Connect pairs of identical numbers with non-crossing, non-branching paths
- **Hashiwokakero** – Connect island nodes with 1–2 bridges; all islands connected; bridges cannot cross
- **Pencils** – Draw lines from pencil tips through cells; pencil length and line length governed by numbers

### C. Cell Shading/Painting
Puzzles where the solver colors or fills cells black/white.

#### C1. Shading with Number Clues (Counting Adjacent/Visible Black Cells)
- **Kurotto** – Circle numbers indicate sum of sizes of contiguous black groups touching the circle
- **Kurodoko** – Numbers indicate count of visible white cells in four directions until a black cell or edge
- **Nurikabe** – Numbers define sizes of white islands; black cells form a connected wall with no 2×2 blocks
- **Akari** – Place light bulbs that illuminate along rows/columns; numbered black cells constrain adjacent bulb count
- **Usowan** – Numbers show adjacent colored cell count, but exactly one number per room is wrong

#### C2. Shading with Region/Shape Constraints
- **Heyawake** – Shade cells in rooms with count constraints; no adjacent black cells; white cells connected; white can't span 3+ rooms in a line
- **Norinori** – Exactly two black cells per region, each part of a domino
- **LITS** – Place one tetromino per region; same-shape tetrominoes can't touch; all colored cells connected; no 2×2 black blocks
- **Nurimisaki** – Cells with circles must be white promontories; no 2×2 same-color blocks; white connected
- **Nuritwin** – Each region has exactly two same-sized shaded blocks; all shaded cells globally connected; no 2×2 shading
- **Choco Banana** – Black groups must form rectangles/squares; white groups must not form rectangles/squares; numbers indicate area size
- **Sto-stone** – Shade cells in rooms per number clues; black cells don't connect across rooms; when "dropped" they fill bottom half of grid
- **Tilepaint** – Color entire tiles or leave them blank; diagonal-cell numbers constrain black cell counts in rows/columns
- **Nurimeizu** – Paint entire rooms to create a maze from S to G; circles on shortest path, triangles not; no 2×2 same-color blocks

#### C3. Shading with Duplicate Elimination
- **Hitori** – Shade cells to eliminate duplicate numbers in rows/columns; no adjacent black cells; white cells connected

#### C4. Shading with Symbol Placement
- **Shakashaka** – Place triangles in cells so remaining white areas form rectangles/squares; numbers constrain adjacent triangle count
- **Juosan** – Fill every cell with — or |; territory numbers constrain the difference; consecutive same-symbol limits apply

### D. Grid Division/Partitioning
Puzzles where the solver divides the grid into regions or blocks.

#### D1. Division into Specific Shapes
- **Shikaku** – Divide grid into rectangles; each contains exactly one number equal to its area
- **Five Cells** – Divide grid into pentominoes; numbers indicate surrounding block-boundary line count
- **Sashigane** – Divide grid into L-shaped blocks; circles mark bends; arrows mark ends pointing toward bends
- **Double Choco** – Divide grid so each block has matching white and gray sub-regions of identical shape

#### D2. Division with Number Filling
- **Fillomino** – Fill grid with numbers and partition into polyominoes where each block's size equals its number; same-size blocks can't touch

### E. Number/Symbol Placement
Puzzles where the solver fills cells with numbers or symbols.

#### E1. Latin-Square Variants
- **Sudoku** – Place 1–9 in each row, column, and 3×3 box

#### E2. Room-Based Number Filling
- **Makaro** – Fill rooms with 1 to N (room size); arrow cells point to the largest neighbor; same numbers can't be adjacent across rooms
- **Ripple Effect** – Fill rooms with 1 to N; repeated numbers in a row/column must be spaced apart by at least the number's value

#### E3. Number Placement by External List
- **Nansuke** – Fill blank cells with digits to form numbers from a given list, crossword-style

### F. Object Placement/Movement
Puzzles where the solver places or moves objects on the grid.

#### F1. Placement
- **Akari** *(also in C1)* – Place light bulbs in white cells subject to illumination and adjacency constraints
- **Hebi** – Place snakes (sequences 1–5) in white cells; snakes can't touch; line-of-sight attack constraint
- **Evolomino** – Place squares to form blocks along arrows; each subsequent block on an arrow grows by one cell without rotation

#### F2. Movement
- **Satogaeri** – Move circles within countries so each country has exactly one; movement distance matches circle number; paths can't cross
- **Yosenabe** – Move all circles straight into gray areas; arrows can't cross or pass over other circles; gray area numbers equal sum of entering circles

### G. Hybrid: Shading + Other Structural Constraint
- **Chained Block** – Shade cells into blocks; each block contains its size number; all blocks must be chained (corner-touching); no duplicate size/shape within a chain

---

## II. By Constraint Mechanism

### Connectivity Constraints
*White or black cells must form a connected network:*
Heyawake, Hitori, Kurodoko, Nurikabe, Nurimisaki, Nuritwin, LITS, Nurimeizu, Usowan

### No 2×2 Block Constraints
*Shaded or unshaded cells cannot form 2×2 squares:*
Nurikabe, Nurimisaki, Nuritwin, LITS, Nurimeizu, Sto-stone

### Adjacency Prohibition (Same-Color/Black)
*Black/colored cells cannot share edges:*
Hitori, Heyawake, Usowan, Yajilin, Norinori (implicitly—dominoes only)

### Room/Region-Based Constraints
*Grid is pre-divided into rooms that govern local rules:*
Heyawake, Double Choco, Makaro, Ripple Effect, Moon-or-Sun, Dotchi-Loop, Nuritwin, Nurimeizu, Juosan, Sto-stone, Usowan, Suraromu, Tilepaint, Norinori, LITS

### Visibility/Line-of-Sight Constraints
*Clues reference what can be "seen" along rows/columns:*
Akari, Kurodoko, Hebi, Yajilin

### Shape Constraints
*Specific geometric shapes must or must not be formed:*
Choco Banana (rectangles vs. non-rectangles), Shakashaka (white rectangles), Sashigane (L-shapes), Shikaku (rectangles), LITS (tetrominoes), Five Cells (pentominoes), Evolomino (growing polyominoes)

---

## III. By Information Type of Given Clues

### Numeric Clues (Counting)
Akari, Kurodoko, Kurotto, Heyawake, Nurikabe, Shakashaka, Slitherlink, Five Cells, Shikaku, Fillomino, Choco Banana, Nurimisaki, Yajilin, Usowan, Sto-stone, Nuritwin, Tilepaint

### Symbolic/Geometric Clues (Circles, Arrows, Symbols)
Masyu (black/white circles), Dotchi-Loop (circles), Mid-loop (black circles), Moon-or-Sun (moon/sun symbols), Makaro (arrows), Sashigane (arrows, open circles), Nagareru (wind arrows), Pencils (triangle tips, arrows), Evolomino (arrows), Hebi (numbered arrows)

### Pre-filled Numbers (to be preserved or deduplicated)
Hitori, Sudoku, Nansuke, Numberlink, Hashiwokakero, Satogaeri, Yosenabe

### Mixed Clues (Numbers + Wildcards)
Chained Block (numbers and "?" marks)
